root.label: Condition variables and waiting
root.note: Sleep until mutex-guarded state changes, rechecking a predicate on every wake; C++20 adds lighter primitives.

children.label: wait semantics
children.note: Atomically unlock and block, then relock before returning.

children.label: Spurious wakeups
children.note: wait may return without any notify, so the predicate must be rechecked.

children.label: Predicate overload
children.note: wait(lock, pred) is while (!pred()) wait(lock); it returns at once if pred is true.

children.label: unique_lock only
children.note: condition_variable takes unique_lock<mutex>; a lock_guard cannot be unlocked by wait.

children.label: One mutex
children.note: All threads waiting at the same time must pass the same mutex, or behavior is undefined.

children.label: Notification
children.note: A notify is a nudge, never stored; with no waiter it does nothing.

children.label: Lost wakeup
children.note: Changing the predicate without the mutex lets a notify land between check and sleep.

children.label: Atomic is not enough
children.note: An atomic flag avoids a data race but not the lost wakeup; take the mutex to change it.

children.label: Notify under lock
children.note: Correct either way; under the lock also keeps a waiter from destroying the cv too early.

children.label: condition_variable_any
children.note: Works with any BasicLockable, such as shared_lock, at some extra cost.

children.label: Stop-aware waits
children.note: C++20 wait(lock, stoken, pred) wakes on stop requests and returns pred().

children.label: False means stopped
children.note: A false result means stop was requested while the predicate still did not hold.

children.label: Timed waits
children.note: wait_for and wait_until bound the sleep; timeouts may always be late.

children.label: cv_status
children.note: Bare timed waits return timeout or no_timeout; no_timeout includes spurious wakes.

children.label: Predicate on timeout
children.note: Predicate forms return the predicate's value at the deadline, not simply false.

children.label: Clocks
children.note: wait_for uses steady_clock; a system_clock deadline follows wall-clock adjustments.

children.label: C++20 primitives
children.note: Mutex-free tools for patterns a condition variable expresses clumsily.

children.label: atomic::wait
children.note: Blocks while the value equals old; returns at once if it differs; never spuriously unchanged.

children.label: counting_semaphore
children.note: acquire and release a counter; no owner, so any thread may release.

children.label: latch
children.note: Single-use countdown; going below zero is undefined; try_wait may rarely report false.

children.label: barrier
children.note: Reusable phases; a noexcept completion step runs once per phase on an arriving thread.

children.label: Choosing
children.note: Pick the narrowest primitive that expresses the wait.

children.label: Arbitrary state
children.note: Use a condition_variable with a predicate under the guarding mutex.

children.label: One result
children.note: Use a future when waiting for a single value or exception.
